hide/causal: A causal model like GPT predicts each token from the ones before it. To predict sat, it may use the and cat, and nothing after.
hide/mask: A masked language model, like BERT, is trained differently. Pick about fifteen percent of the tokens, hide each behind a mask token, and train the model to recover them.
hide/both: It has no causal mask: every position attends to every other. So to recover sat, it reads the and cat on the left, and on, a, mat on the right.
hide/count: Only the hidden tokens are scored. In a sequence of two hundred tokens, fifteen percent is thirty: thirty losses, where a causal model gets two hundred.
jobs/attend: In attention terms: in a sequence of six, position two of a causal model attends to three positions, itself and the two before it. In a masked model, it attends to all six.
jobs/generate: Generating text means writing one token at a time, with nothing yet on the right. That is exactly the causal model's training task, so causal models are the ones that write.
jobs/fill: Filling in a blank in the middle of a sentence, with words on both sides, is the masked model's task.
